nexis 0.3.0 adds instants and UUIDs as real values with Clojure's `#inst` and `#uuid` literals, and gives macros `&form` and `&env`. It also brings a review of the whole codebase. That review fixed about twenty bugs, including crashes, memory-safety errors and wrong database answers, made several slow paths hundreds of times faster, and cut the source from 82,500 to about 71,500 lines. Of the cut, roughly 4,300 lines moved into the test suites and the rest were deleted.

## Changes that need attention

- **Nextomic instants and UUIDs are values.** `:db.type/instant` takes and returns an `inst` (`#inst "…"`, `nexis.time/now`), and `:db.type/uuid` takes and returns a `uuid` (`#uuid "…"`, `random-uuid`, `parse-uuid`), as Datomic does with a `Date` and a `UUID`. A long or a string written to these attributes is now `:nextomic/value-type`. Wrap the value with `(nexis.time/instant ms)` or `(parse-uuid s)`. The stored bytes do not change: stores written by 0.2.0 open in 0.3.0, and the reverse.
- **`random-uuid` returns a uuid, and `uuid?` is true only of a uuid.** `str` of a uuid gives the canonical text. The `nexis.time.Instant` record is gone; `nexis.time` makes and takes the `inst` kind.
- **JSON's position in its own text** is reported as `:json-line` and `:json-column`. `:line` and `:column` now name the program's place, as every other caught error does.
- **Codec decode errors.** Stored bytes that do not decode are `:codec-failed`. Encoding an unserializable value is still `:unserializable`.
- **Multimethod metadata.** A multimethod keeps its dispatch table in its own metadata, under `:multifn-state`, so `(meta mm)` is no longer nil, and `with-meta` of a multimethod returns a plain function.
- **Small Clojure-fidelity changes:**
  - a repeated `letfn` name is its last binding;
  - `#!` is a comment anywhere;
  - `db/open` refuses options it does not take;
  - the regex repetition bound of 1000 is gone.

## What is new

- **`#inst` and `#uuid`.** Both read, print as Clojure prints them, and round-trip through `pr-str`, `read-string`, `nexis.edn`, durable refs and JSON.
  - An `inst` compares and sorts by its milliseconds.
  - A `uuid` orders as its text does.
  - `random-uuid` draws from the process's secure random source.
- **`&form` and `&env` in macros.** These follow Clojure's convention:
  - `&form` is the call, with its `:line`/`:column`;
  - `&env` is the locals in scope;
  - `macroexpand` passes a nil `&env`;
  - arity errors count only the user's arguments.
- **Closer to Clojure:**
  - `upper-case`/`lower-case` map every Unicode character as Java's `Character` does;
  - functions carry metadata;
  - `clojure.core` names `nexis.core`;
  - the transducer arities of `take-nth`, `replace`, `random-sample` and `partitionv-all`;
  - `thrown-with-msg?`;
  - `run-tests` of several namespaces;
  - `defonce` and `merge` as Clojure has them.
- **I/O.**
  - `spit` writes as a stream, so pipes and FIFOs work, and `:append` opens with O_APPEND, so concurrent appenders don't overwrite each other.
  - `slurp`/`spit` take `:encoding "UTF-8"`.
  - JSON escapes U+2028 and U+2029.
  - `nano-time` counts 64 bits.
- **Errors.**
  - Every error a library function raises carries the place keys.
  - Every Nextomic query and pull refusal names the rule, variable, symbol or attribute at fault.
  - `macroexpand-1` says why a macro failed.

## Fixed

- **Crashes:**
  - `foo./bar`;
  - nested lookup refs thousands deep;
  - a program rebinding `realize-caught`;
  - damaged store files, which now give `:db/corrupted` instead of a crash or silent wrong answers.
- **Garbage-collection rooting gaps**, reachable from ordinary programs:
  - `reduce` over a `cycle`;
  - `string/join` of a map;
  - `conj` of lazy keys into a transient;
  - `into` a hash map from a map;
  - a lazy sequence whose body forces itself, which now raises `:stack-overflow`.
- **Nextomic:**
  - an upsert through a lookup ref to an explicit eid or unique value;
  - schema attributes on non-attribute entities, and renaming a bootstrap ident (renaming `:db/fulltext` silently dropped every fulltext flag);
  - a nil element in a relation binding.
- **Error handling:** a caught error reaches its handler even when the heap is exhausted.
- **Memory:** `db/open`/`db/close` no longer leak, and an unreachable multimethod is collected.
- **Printing:** a protocol prints its name.
- **Docs:** removing a library Var's `:doc` with `reset-meta!` sticks.

## Faster

- **Nextomic queries** (Debug-build probes, before → after):

  | Workload | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8,000-element set constant | 16.6 s | 20 ms |
  | 8,000 rules | 686 ms | 53 ms |
  | 9,000 rule calls | 1.27 GB | 101 MB |
  | 4,000 `not` clauses | 280 MB | 55 MB |

- **Long decimal integers** parse by divide and conquer: 400,000 digits in 121 ms, where it took 1.15 s.
- **Collections:**
  - persistent vector `pop` is 30% fewer instructions;
  - map and set literals of up to eight entries skip hashing and sorting;
  - 37 pure natives are leaf calls.

## Smaller

The source is about 71,500 lines, against 82,500 in 0.2.0. The VM's main file went from 10,770 to 8,450 lines; the cut includes duplicated tests, comments that restated the specs, and repeated code. Store-backed test suites moved out of `src/` into `test/integration/`. Hot paths were measured before and after each change.

## Known gaps

- One thread: no `future`, `pmap`, agents or STM.
- No package manager, and no server mode.
- `as-of` of an instant (TODO #22).
- A durable commit writes more pages than Datalevin's (PERF §3.39).
- A core function called through its Var pays a full call (TODO #19).

The full list is in [TODO.md](https://github.com/shreeve/nexis/blob/v0.3.0/TODO.md).

## Platforms

These are the same as for 0.2.0: static `x86_64-linux-musl` and `aarch64-linux-musl`, and `aarch64-macos`. Each archive, `nexis-0.3.0-TARGET.tar.gz`, holds `bin/nexis`, the README, the LICENSE and `BUILD-INFO`, and `SHA256SUMS` lists their checksums. The binary has emdb compiled in; emdb's source is not public.
